content: 1. Budesonide affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which can decrease the levels or effects of darunavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Dasatinib increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while budesonide decreases the levels or effects of dasatinib through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Deferasirox reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Additionally, deferasirox has been associated with gastric ulceration and gastrointestinal bleeding. Caution is advised when co-administering with drugs that increase the risk of peptic ulcers or gastric hemorrhage, including corticosteroids. 4. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Dexlansoprazole reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, potentially altering the drug's release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 6. DHEA (herbal) increases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Both dichlorphenamide and budesonide decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Diclofenac and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 9. Diflunisal and budesonide may also increase each other's toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism, with a heightened risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 11. Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 12. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases its levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored if co-administered. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 13. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of eletriptan by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Eliglustat increases the levels of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Therapeutic drug concentrations should be monitored, or the dosage of the P-gp substrate should be reduced and titrated to clinical effect. 15. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have elevated plasma concentrations associated with serious or life-threatening events. 16. Encorafenib affects CYP3A4 metabolism and both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Budesonide and enoxaparin require caution and monitoring. Corticosteroids may decrease anticoagulant effects by increasing blood coagulability, but they may also impair vascular integrity, increasing bleeding risk. INR should be closely monitored. 18. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of erlotinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases the levels or effects of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 20. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Esomeprazole reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, potentially altering the drug's release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 22. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of estradiol, conjugated synthetic estrogens, and estropipate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Etodolac and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 24. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases the levels or effects of budesonide through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are required. 25. Famotidine reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, potentially altering the drug's release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 26. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 27. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of felodipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while felodipine increases the levels or effects of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 28. Fenoprofen and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Budesonide increases the effects of fingolimod through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Concomitant therapy is expected to heighten the risk of immunosuppression. Caution is advised when switching patients from long-acting therapies with immune effects. 30. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 31. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Flurbiprofen and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 33. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 34. Budesonide and fondaparinux require caution and monitoring. Corticosteroids may decrease anticoagulant effects by increasing blood coagulability, but they may also impair vascular integrity, increasing bleeding risk. INR should be closely monitored. 35. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while budesonide decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 36. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 37. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 40. Budesonide decreases the effects of Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Vaccination should be avoided during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible, as the antibody response may be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence has been restored. 41. Budesonide and heparin require caution and monitoring. Corticosteroids may decrease anticoagulant effects by increasing blood coagulability, but they may also impair vascular integrity, increasing bleeding risk. INR should be closely monitored. 42. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 43. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Ibuprofen and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 45. Ibuprofen IV and budesonide may also increase each other's toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism, with a heightened risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Ibuprofen/famotidine reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, potentially altering the drug's release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 47. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Corticosteroids may be needed to treat severe diarrhea or colitis associated with idelalisib therapy. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are known to increase systemic exposure to oral budesonide. Close monitoring for increased systemic corticosteroid effects is necessary. 48. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of iloperidone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while iloperidone increases the levels of budesonide through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are required. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 49. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Indomethacin and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 51. Budesonide decreases the effects of influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, recombinant) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are required. The immune response to the vaccine may be reduced in immunocompromised individuals. 52. Budesonide decreases the effects of influenza virus vaccine (trivalent, recombinant) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are required. The immune response to the vaccine may be reduced in immunocompromised individuals. 53. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 54. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 and P-gp substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates should be considered. 55. Ivacaftor increases the levels of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite have the potential to inhibit P-gp, which may significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 56. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of budesonide by influencing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreasing metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 57. Ketoprofen and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Ketorolac and budesonide may also increase each other's toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism, with a heightened risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Ketorolac intranasal and budesonide may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 60. Lansoprazole reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary.
